description: Cursor's official .rpm on Fedora, and one artifact serving both distro families.
why: Two things at once. The identifier: rpm_packages `cursor`, read off a real rpm install rather than assumed to equal the deb's name. And the artifact: dist/discovery-linux.sql names deb_packages AND rpm_packages, and this is the run where the ABSENT one has to return no rows instead of erroring the whole statement -- which is what a genuinely missing table does, as `snap_packages` demonstrates by returning [] and exit 1 on every Linux box. `deb` is pinned at >=0 here for exactly that reason, and it is the assertion, not an omission.
known_gaps: Runs in Rocky 9, Fedora 41 and Amazon Linux 2023 containers on an ubuntu runner, because GitHub offers no RPM-distro runner. A container has no systemd, so `unit` is 0 here and the systemd marker reports absent -- correctly. test/run-gce.sh runs it on a Rocky 9 VM and test/run-ec2.sh on Amazon Linux 2023 instances, where it is not.
